science.title: Comparison of NASM Corrective Exercise Alone Versus with Kinesio Taping on Navicular Drop and Lower Limb Function in Female Adolescents with Flexible Flatfoot: A Randomized Clinical Trial
science.description: Functional flatfoot is a common condition in adolescents that can impair postural control and increase the risk of lower limb injuries, making effective management important. This randomized clinical trial examined the effects of an eight-week National Academy of Sports Medicine (NASM) corrective exercise program, with and without Kinesio taping, on clinical and functional outcomes in adolescents with functional flatfoot. Forty-five female adolescents aged 13 to 16 years with a navicular drop ≥ 10 mm were randomly assigned to three groups: NASM corrective exercise, NASM corrective exercise plus Kinesio taping, and control. Primary outcomes were navicular drop, assessed with the Navicular Drop Test (NDT), and lower limb function, measured using the Manchester Oxford Foot Questionnaire (MOXFQ). Secondary outcomes included dynamic balance, evaluated by the Y-Balance Test, and ankle proprioception. Results showed that both intervention groups achieved significant improvements in NDT, function, balance, and proprioception compared with the control group (p = 0.001), confirming the effectiveness of NASM corrective exercise. However, no additional benefits were observed when Kinesio taping was combined with corrective exercise (p > 0.05). These findings suggest that NASM corrective exercise alone is a practical, non-invasive, and cost-effective intervention for improving foot posture, functional performance, and balance in adolescents with functional flatfoot. science.title: Enhancement of thiourea leaching performance of refractory silver tailings by mechanical activation
science.description: Refractory silver tailings are both an environmental liability and a potential secondary resource for precious metals. However, strong mineralogical locking of silver-bearing phases within barite and aluminosilicate matrices severely limits silver recovery under conventional leaching conditions. In this study, mechanical activation was investigated as a pretreatment method to enhance the thiourea leaching performance of refractory silver tailings from the Kütahya Eti Silver Plant (Turkey). Mechanical activation was carried out in a planetary ball mill for 0, 30, 60, and 90 min. The resulting changes in particle size, specific surface area, and structure were evaluated by particle size analysis, BET, XRD, and SEM. Mechanical activation caused marked particle fragmentation, increased surface area, and partial amorphization, indicating enhanced structural disorder and improved accessibility of silver-bearing phases. Thiourea leaching experiments were performed using 0.5 M thiourea in acidic solution at pH 1.5, with 0.01 M ferric sulfate as the oxidizing agent. Under the optimum conditions identified in this study, namely 90 min mechanical activation, 50 °C, S/L = 1/10, and 600 rpm, silver recovery increased from about 68% for the non-activated sample to about 96% for the mechanically activated sample. Kinetic analysis under conditions minimizing external mass-transfer resistance showed that apparent rate constants increased with activation time, while the apparent activation energy decreased from 46.1 to 38.9 kJ·mol−1. Post-leaching SEM and BET results revealed agglomerated and porous particle structures, indicating that diffusion through evolving porous particle assemblies contributes to the observed kinetic behavior. This work directly links mechanochemically induced structural evolution with apparent leaching kinetics in industrial refractory silver tailings and highlights mechanically assisted thiourea leaching as a promising cyanide-free alternative for refractory silver-bearing wastes.

science.title: This food compound may help vaccines work better in older adults
science.description: A naturally occurring compound found in foods such as wheat germ, mushrooms, and aged cheese may help older adults build stronger protection after vaccination. In a small pilot trial, researchers gave spermidine supplements to adults over 65 following their third COVID-19 vaccine dose. The biggest improvements appeared among people whose immune systems initially responded poorly, with higher antibody levels and stronger activity against several variants.

science.title: Dying Sun-like stars may kick themselves through space
science.description: Dying Sun-like stars may not fade away quietly. As blobs of gas erupt unevenly from their swollen surfaces, each burst gives the star a tiny push in the opposite direction. Thousands of these random kicks could eventually break apart distant stellar pairs or, in rare cases, drive two stars into a violent collision.

ai.title: Anthropic Gets US Court Nod for $1.5 Bn AI Copyright Lawsuit Settlement
ai.description: A US federal judge granted final approval to Anthropic's $1.5 billion settlement in a copyright class action brought by a group of authors, marking the largest publicly known settlement in a US copyright case. The ruling brings one of the first major AI copyright disputes in the United States closer to a conclusion, although separate lawsuits by authors who opted out of the settlement remain pending. US District Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin in San Francisco approved the settlement on Monday, rejecting objections from some authors who argued that the compensation was inadequate and that the plaintiffs' lawyers would receive an excessive share of the payout, as per Reuters. The judge concluded that concerns over the settlement amount were "not grounded in a realistic assessment of the overall risks and rewards of a trial," Reuters reported.
